meta.name: Coachify
meta.description: A profitable, top-rated AI fitness coaching app with $70K MRR, 14 months of proven paid UA, and a loyal subscriber base — ready for a strategic acquirer to unlock its next phase of scale.

product.vision: Coachify is building the AI personal trainer for the 80% of gym-goers who train without a coach — delivering professional-grade programming, nutrition guidance, and real-time feedback at a fraction of the cost of a human trainer.

roadmap.description: Integrated diet monitoring with food database and AI-generated meal suggestions.

opportunities.description: Systematic testing of pricing tiers, trial lengths, and offer structures. Conservative 15–20% improvement in trial-to-paid conversion is achievable within 90 days.

opportunities.title: TikTok Organic + Paid UA
opportunities.description: With 99.7K TikTok followers and zero paid spend on the platform, there is a clear path to a new high-volume acquisition channel.

opportunities.title: Apple Search Ads
opportunities.description: The app ranks for 1,249 keywords but runs zero Apple Search Ads. Launching campaigns could deliver the lowest-CAC installs available.

opportunities.title: International Expansion
opportunities.description: App is predominantly English-language. Localization into Spanish, Portuguese, and German markets represents a near-zero COGS growth lever.

processSteps.description: Includes Meta Ads Manager screenshots, RevenueCat dashboards, cohort exports, P&L, tech stack, and seller Q&A.

processSteps.title: Submit Offer
processSteps.description: Best and final offers accepted on a rolling basis. We recommend acting within 14 days — active buyer interest is high.

news.title: How Jane Doe built and sold Notey for $2.4M
news.subtitle: Jane Doe never planned to sell Notey. The note-taking app started as a weekend project in her Berlin apartment, a simple tool she built because nothing on the market worked the way she wanted it to.
news.quote: I thought selling an app meant posting it on a marketplace and hoping for the best. EHVM showed me there's a proper way to do this — with the right buyers, the right terms, and the right support.

news.subtitle: One started as a side project by Max Man, a Copenhagen-based developer who wanted a meditation app that didn't feel like a Silicon Valley product. No gamification, no streaks, no push notifications begging you to come back. Just guided sessions and silence.
news.quote: What made EHVM different is they didn't just find any buyer — they found the right buyer. Someone who saw the same value in the product that I did.

story.headline: The story behind EHVM Apps Capital test

blocks.content: EHVM Apps Capital was founded by Evelin Herrera with a simple idea: create a space where app builders and buyers can connect directly, without the noise. A marketplace built by someone who understands both sides of the table.

Before starting EHVM, Evelin spent years building and scaling mobile apps across industries — from wellness to fintech. She saw firsthand how difficult it was for independent developers to find the right exit, and how hard it was for buyers to discover quality apps with real traction.

blocks.quoteText: I kept meeting incredible builders who had no idea what their app was worth, and buyers who couldn't find what they were looking for. EHVM is the bridge.

blocks.content: Today, EHVM curates a portfolio of high-quality apps with verified metrics — monthly recurring revenue, user acquisition data, platform details, and growth potential. Every listing is vetted. Every transaction is supported.
Whether you're a developer ready to move on to your next project, or an entrepreneur looking to acquire a proven product — EHVM is where it happens.
